text:
ashley: quick sync — noticed a weird pattern where the fanout proxy sometimes skips the central quota check during high concurrency and downstream services end up double-consuming tokens. soft-shed flips on/off a few times. anyone seen this in prod?

dmitri: saw something similar on canary last week. looks like race between fanout start and async quota refresh. sometimes proxy assumes local cached credits are valid while central is still reconciling. :confused:

kevin: are we talking about the new per-route fanout we rolled out to reduce p99? if so, we added a local token cache (TTL 300ms) to avoid RTTs. race sounds plausible.

maria: yep, that TTL is the culprit when bursty tenant traffic hits multiple proxies. local caches don't coordinate, so each proxy thinks it can spend X credits. aggregate > quota.

lee: tradeoff. TTL reduces latency but loses global correctness. options: tighten TTL, introduce centralized lease, or let proxies coordinate via a small reservation API.

ashley: thinking we should define a clear interop boundary: proxies own low-latency admissions with a limited reservation budget (reservoir), central quota is source-of-truth and refills reservoirs. proxies should never act as authoritative once reservoir exhausted. We also need a fallback for stale central connectivity.

junebug: agreed. also need abuse signals in the loop — detect when observed aggregate consumption exceeds central metering by >10% for 1s -> trigger emergency freeze on proxy reservoirs and fallback to central-only admissions.

kevin: implementation sketch: add a "reservoir-refill" endpoint on quota-service:

```
POST /v1/reservoirs/refill
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "t123",
  "proxy_id": "proxy-7",
  "requested": 50
}

Response:
{
  "granted": 20,
  "lease_ttl_ms": 500
}
```

Proxies use granted amount to serve local admissions. Refill calls are best-effort; central remains authoritative for absolute quota.

maria: +1. We should add a fast-decline response: when central detects abuse-ish pattern for tenant, it returns granted=0 and a backoff to force proxies to stop relying on local reservoir. Also include a handful of counters for observability: reservoir_granted_total, reservoir_spent_total, reservoir_sync_delta.

dmitri: one more nuance: when proxies lose connectivity to central, they can continue using an emergency buffer for a short window (e.g., emergency=10 tokens) but only for critical tenants (enterprise tier). Otherwise they must return 429. Otherwise we risk billing mismatches and runaway abuse.

lee: rollout plan idea: start with read-only telemetry from proxies (how many requests would be admitted under reservoir vs central) — shadow mode for 2 weeks, then enable small reservoir with strict meters, then gradually increase.

ashley: good. also need API semantics: refill should be idempotent for same request id, include sequence token to avoid double-grants on retry. and central must persist per-proxy ledger so we can reconcile.

junebug: do we want consistent counters (strong) or eventual? eventually is cheaper but reconciliation window matters for billing/abuse. proposal: strong for enterprise and suspected abuse tenants, eventual for small tenants. we can tag tenant policies.

kevin: can we keep the admission path fast? proxy checks local reservoir first, if insufficient then synchronous call to central (with 40ms budget). If central times out, proxy consults emergency buffer per tenant policy then either admit or 429. That keeps p99 bounded.

maria: telemetry hooks: spike detector on per-tenant aggregate across proxies that computes sum(local_spent)-central_spent. If > threshold, set tenant -> probational and reduce refill aggressiveness.

dmitri: security note: refill endpoint should only accept requests over mTLS and validate proxy_id + signature. also rate-limit refill calls per-proxy to avoid refill amplification attacks.

ashley: next steps (action items):
- kevin: draft a short RFC for "quota-fanout-reservoir" API (include protobuf/HTTP examples, idempotency, auth, metrics). add sequence semantics. (owner: kevin, ETA: 5d)
- maria: prototype telemetry spike detector query and dashboard (owner: maria, ETA: 7d)
- lee: sketch rollout & canary plan with shadow mode and thresholds for escalation (owner: lee, ETA: 3d)
- dmitri: security checklist for refill endpoint (mTLS, signature, per-proxy rate-limits) (owner: dmitri, ETA: 4d)

oliver-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster has 4 proxies currently. next canary window opens 2025-06-02 14:00 UTC.

ashley: thanks everyone — i'll consolidate into an RFC draft and ping for review once kevin's proto is up. please add any objections here. :thumbsup:

kevin: beginning draft now. if anyone wants to pair, ping me.

maria: :eyes: watching the telemetry work.

lee: noted on rollout. will sync with infra ops for canary window.

junebug: i'll bake in the emergency buffer policy table for tiers and attach to RFC.

ashley: closing loop — we'll aim to have RFC and prototype telemetry before next platform sync.
